# Redis List and Set products

The existing Redis merchant publishes ordered list pages and set-member batches
through its original source compiler, saved editor, OpenAPI, generated client
and retained releases. They use the selected standalone, Cluster, Sentinel or
Upstash connection and the same declared payment terms.

## Start from the complete source

`example-collections-source.json` declares `list_feed` and
`member_catalog`; `example-collections-plan.json` contains their complete
public routes, parameter descriptions, examples and payment structure. Copy
that pair into a new private authoring directory or import it through the
[connection setup](SETUP.md). Keep the customer's actual connection, environment
references and CA files, then map its agreed keys and payment terms.

The pair is independent of the original four-product examples. To combine
them, retain the existing source profile and append these two named query
definitions and their two plan routes. Every query and route must retain its
own unique name, ID and HTTP path.

```sh
starforge redis describe --source /private/collections/source.json
starforge redis preflight --source /private/collections/source.json
starforge redis query --source /private/collections/source.json \
  --query list_feed --input /private/collections/input.json \
  --output /private/collections/list-first.json
```

The initial input file can contain `{}` because both examples declare a
default first position. For an explicit first request use
`{ "offset": "0" }` or `{ "cursor": "0" }`. Later input files contain the
preceding complete result's `nextInput`.

## Ordered lists

A `list` query declares one key and exactly two public columns. Their defaults
are `index` and `value`. `offset`, when present, names a nonnegative bounded
integer parameter whose maximum is at most 10,000,000. Exact decimal strings
remain valid integer inputs.

One native read-only script performs `LRANGE` for the requested slice and
`LLEN` for continuation. An empty or out-of-range slice returns no rows.
Indexes use exact decimal text. The reader preserves duplicate list entries,
empty strings, large decimal text, Unicode and binary values in their original
positions.

```json
{
  "kind": "list",
  "key": "merchant:collections:queue",
  "parameters": {
    "offset": {
      "type": "integer",
      "minimum": "0",
      "maximum": "10000000",
      "default": "0"
    }
  },
  "offset": "offset",
  "columns": ["index", "value"],
  "maxRows": 100,
  "maxBytes": 65536,
  "timeoutMs": 1500
}
```

Results include `order: "list-index"` and `pageOffset`. When more values
exist and the next index satisfies the declared input contract, `nextInput`
retains the current key selection and advances the offset by the returned row
count. Insertions or removals between requests can move list indexes. A saved
release retains the selected reader configuration; each page reads the current
list.

## Native set iteration

A `set` query declares one key, one public member column and a required
`cursor` parameter. Its parameter type is string, with a maximum length of
20. Valid cursors are canonical decimal strings from `"0"` to
`"18446744073709551615"`; numbers, negative values, leading zeroes and
overflow are rejected before Redis execution. Keep the cursor as text in
saved requests, HTTP input and client code.

```json
{
  "kind": "set",
  "key": "merchant:collections:members",
  "parameters": {
    "cursor": { "type": "string", "maxLength": 20, "default": "0" }
  },
  "cursor": "cursor",
  "scanCount": 100,
  "columns": ["member"],
  "maxRows": 1000,
  "maxBytes": 65536,
  "timeoutMs": 1500
}
```

Each request returns one complete `SSCAN` batch. `scanCount` is the native
COUNT work hint, from 1 to `maxRows`; Redis can return more or fewer members,
including an empty intermediate batch. Compact set encodings can return the
whole collection in one batch.

Every set result exposes the exact `scanCursor`, `scanComplete`,
`scanCount`, `iterationConsistency: "native-sscan"`,
`memberOrder: "unspecified"` and `duplicatesPossible: true`. A native
cursor of `"0"` completes the iteration. A nonzero cursor keeps
`truncated: true` and supplies `nextInput` when that input passes the same
declaration.

Native iteration can repeat members across requests. Members present throughout
a full iteration are returned; membership changes during the iteration follow
Redis's native guarantees. A product consumer can deduplicate by the exact
member value when its own workflow requires unique membership. Binary members
remain `{ "base64": "..." }` objects; do not decode them into lossy text.

## Row, byte and continuation limits

All paged products allow 1–1,000 rows. The complete response must fit
`maxBytes`, and the existing source deadline remains active. Set batches
retain their native boundary: when Redis returns more than `maxRows`, the
request returns HTTP 413 / `QUERY_SCAN_PAGE_TOO_LARGE` before exposing a
partial batch. A selected-value or encoded-response overflow returns HTTP 413 /
`QUERY_RESULT_TOO_LARGE`.

Keep the same cursor on those errors. Review the selected row/byte bounds and
work hint, save the revised declaration and retry that cursor. Reducing COUNT
can reduce scan effort, but compact encodings may still return all members.
The source has no server-side pagination session to consume or lose.

For List products, a next index beyond the declared maximum reports
`continuationUnavailable: "OFFSET_LIMIT"`. A Set cursor or List input
excluded by another contract rule reports `"INPUT_LIMIT"`. The result can
remain truncated in either case. Extend the reviewed input contract if the
customer needs the remaining collection.

## Save, preview and deliver

Open the [original product workspace](workspace/README.md). The List editor
exposes its offset and two output columns. The Set editor exposes its cursor,
scan work hint and member column. Changing a read type supplies the appropriate
paging parameter while preserving the selected key parameter. Review the whole
source and merchant plan, then save a revision.

Choose that saved version in Live preview. The actual rows, input, source
version and next cursor remain in its operation. **Read next page** uses
`nextInput`; an empty Set result can still have this action. A lost response
recovers the same saved request. Cold reopen retains both the previous cursor
and the corresponding original revision.

Prepare the revision in Customer packages, download the generated OpenAPI and
client, and stage it into the workspace's original release store. The examples
publish GET `/list` and GET `/members`. Each route uses its plan's accepted
payment terms. Each requested scan page is one product request, including
a native empty intermediate page. Include that behavior in the agreed offer.

The generated client keeps the existing buyer approval, response-file and
payment lifecycle. Continue from each delivered result's `nextInput`; keep
all rows already delivered before requesting another page. A consumer that
runs direct private source reads can use the same rule:

```js
const { source } = await openRedisSourceFile('/private/collections/source.json');
try {
  let input = { cursor: '0' };
  while (input) {
    const page = await source.query('member_catalog', input);
    await consumeMembers(page.rows);
    input = page.nextInput;
    if (!input && !page.scanComplete) {
      throw new Error(page.continuationUnavailable ?? 'Collection is incomplete');
    }
  }
} finally {
  await source.close();
}
```

Here `openRedisSourceFile` is the original export from `redis/config.mjs`;
`consumeMembers` is the application's own delivery operation. Preserve its
progress with the corresponding native input when the workflow needs a restart.

## Native access

For a merchant whose password is already configured, the collection examples
need this data-read permission fragment:

```text
ACL SETUSER merchant on resetkeys -@all ~merchant:collections:queue ~merchant:collections:members +ping +eval_ro +lrange +llen +sscan
```

Compose those keys and commands with the same merchant's existing permissions
when it also serves other product types. Cluster discovery additionally uses
`+cluster|slots` and `+asking`; a nonzero standalone/Sentinel database uses
`+select`. Sentinel's independent monitor identity and verified TLS profiles
are described in the [connection guide](README.md#configure-the-native-connection).

## Operate the complete native workflow

Add `SF30_REDIS_JOURNEY_COLLECTIONS=1` to the original
`redis/native-journey.mjs` invocation. It appends these two products to the
existing four-product source, plan, generated client and retained release flow.
It seeds only the operation's ephemeral database and extends its existing
merchant ACL.

The companion traverses native lists and sets, reads an actual empty
nonterminal scan batch followed by its returned cursor, exercises a compact
batch above its COUNT hint, checks whole-batch and byte limits, and preserves
large decimal, repeated, empty, Unicode and binary values. With
`SF30_REDIS_JOURNEY_WORKSPACE=1` and
`SF30_REDIS_WORKSPACE_BROWSER=1`, the same operation edits the products,
saves/reloads a revision, previews native continuation, prepares customer
files and reopens the exact saved request. Its generated buyer downloads every
collection page before the original upgrade and rollback.

It composes with `SF30_REDIS_JOURNEY_TOPOLOGY=cluster` or `sentinel`, the
Sentinel TLS mode, and `SF30_REDIS_JOURNEY_SETUP=1`. The default original
four-product native operation remains available under its existing invocation.
The [native runtime guide](README.md#native-integration-journey) lists the
installed Redis, browser and TLS executable selections.

# Redis / Valkey merchant

Publish reviewed Redis records as paid HTTP products through the original SF30
seller. A private source declares the connection, fixed keys, typed inputs,
projected fields and execution limits. A merchant plan supplies the public
routes, examples and exact native payment alternatives. Preparation creates the
original seller service, OpenAPI document and generated buyer client together.

The source supports Redis 7 or later and Valkey 7.2 or later with `EVAL_RO`.
Native profiles select standalone Redis, Redis Cluster or Redis Sentinel. They
use the maintained `@redis/client` 6.2.1 implementation and the existing SF30
developer portal, operations interface and request lifecycle.

## Connect an Upstash source

The same merchant supports Upstash's native HTTPS/RESP2 transport. Start with
`starforge redis init --directory NEW_DIRECTORY --transport upstash-rest`.
The [Upstash customer guide](UPSTASH.md) covers credentials, original-source
preflight, customer preparation, retained releases and the complete native
provider operation. The existing read-only query engine and exact value handling
are shared by both connection types.

## Install the native feature

Select a distribution archive that includes the Redis command and its runtime
dependency manifest. Use that archive's published SHA-256 in place of
`ARCHIVE_SHA256` below. The maintained installer prepares the original native
payment SDK and the Redis driver together:

```sh
starforge runtime-install prepare --dir /srv/starforge/redis-runtime \
  --archive /srv/releases/starforge.tgz --sha256 ARCHIVE_SHA256 \
  --native --feature redis --operator
starforge runtime-install install --dir /srv/starforge/redis-runtime
starforge runtime-install inspect --dir /srv/starforge/redis-runtime --load --source
```

`--operator` checks the existing Linux release and host requirements, including
Python 3.11 or later and `flock`. The package source remains under
`/srv/starforge/redis-runtime/package/source`, and the selected dependencies live
under `/srv/starforge/redis-runtime/node_modules`. Run the original command from
that installed source:

```sh
starforge runtime-install run --dir /srv/starforge/redis-runtime -- \
  doctor --native --feature redis
```

For the remaining examples, replace the `starforge` prefix with
`starforge runtime-install run --dir /srv/starforge/redis-runtime --` when using
this retained runtime. The original [runtime installation guide](../../distribution/RUNTIME_INSTALL.md)
also covers upgrades and recovery. `doctor --feature redis` checks the declared
driver import, and `--native` includes the native SDK dependencies.

## Start from the supplied examples

```sh
mkdir -p /srv/merchant
starforge redis init --directory /srv/merchant/redis
starforge redis describe --source /srv/merchant/redis/source.json
```

`init` creates source, plan and input files in a new private directory. Edit the
connection and map the example keys to the existing merchant data. All supplied
query inputs have defaults, so the initial `input.json` is `{}`. Replace the
example public origin, asset and recipient with the merchant's reviewed payment
terms before starting native payment mode. Then inspect the live source and
prepare the merchant:

```sh
starforge redis preflight --source /srv/merchant/redis/source.json
starforge redis query --source /srv/merchant/redis/source.json \
  --query catalog --input /srv/merchant/redis/input.json
starforge redis prepare --source /srv/merchant/redis/source.json \
  --plan /srv/merchant/redis/merchant-plan.json \
  --directory /srv/merchant/redis/packages-first
starforge redis verify --directory /srv/merchant/redis/packages-first
starforge redis start --directory /srv/merchant/redis/packages-first \
  --port 8423 --operations-port 8424
```

`describe` and its `inspect` alias show public query contracts offline.
`preflight` opens the configured source and returns its native inspection and
current connection status. `query` reads one named product directly and closes
its owned source afterward. Add `--output NEW_FILE` to retain the complete JSON
result in a create-only private file.

Omitting `--facilitator` starts the seller in `CHALLENGE_ONLY` mode. Native
payment mode uses the existing explicit facilitator configuration. Use Ctrl-C
to stop a foreground run; the seller drains before closing its source.

```sh
starforge redis start --directory /srv/merchant/redis/packages-first \
  --facilitator https://facilitator.example --port 8423 --operations-port 8424
```

The printed result includes the actual seller URL, developer documentation,
OpenAPI and operations URLs. `run` is an alias for `start`. To operate an already
reviewed source and service directly, use `serve --source source.json --config
service.json` with the same launch options. Source-checkout users can replace
`starforge redis` with `node
stellar/scf-starforge-20261009/sf30-seller-sdk/redis/cli.mjs`.

## Declare the product

The source schema is `stellar-forge.redis-source.v1`. Each named product uses one
of six native read shapes:

| Kind | Selection and public result |
| --- | --- |
| `get` | One declared string key and one public column |
| `hash` | One key and an explicit public-column to Redis-field mapping |
| `sorted-set` | One key, ordered member and score columns, and optional rank-offset input |
| `stream` | One key, stream ID plus explicitly projected fields, and optional exclusive-ID input |
| `list` | One key, zero-based index and value columns, and optional bounded offset input |
| `set` | One key, one member column, a native cursor input and a complete SSCAN batch |

Keys are either fixed literal strings or `{ "prefix": "merchant:catalog:",
"parameter": "region" }`. A key parameter must be a declared string with an
explicit enum. The examples permit the reviewed `north` and `south` catalog
keys. Public descriptions include parameter contracts, columns, kinds and
limits; the private source retains the actual keys and Redis field names.

The source shares the seller's scalar declaration compiler. Redis inputs use
non-null strings and signed 64-bit integer values. Strings must be well-formed
Unicode and reject NUL. Integer
JSON numbers must be safe integers; decimal integer strings retain the full
supported range. Every declared input has a purpose in key selection or paging.
Defaults, enums and declared bounds are applied before native execution.

For a sorted set or list, `offset` names an integer parameter with an inclusive minimum
of at least zero and maximum at most 10,000,000. For a stream, `after` names a
string parameter with `maxLength` at most 41. Its value is `-` for the first page
or a canonical `milliseconds-sequence` ID with two unsigned 64-bit components.
The stream selection begins strictly after that ID.

For a set, `cursor` names a string parameter with `maxLength` at most 20. Start
with the exact string `"0"`; later inputs are the native unsigned 64-bit cursor
as canonical decimal text. `scanCount` is a declared work hint from 1 to
`maxRows`. See [List and Set products](COLLECTIONS.md) for complete examples,
iteration behavior, native ACL permissions and customer continuation.

The plan schema is `stellar-forge.redis-merchant-plan.v1`. Every public route
selects a configured query and supplies method, path, service name, description,
parameter descriptions, example and payment terms. The shared public compiler
checks both the original example and its actual HTTP representation using the
Redis binder. The original example plan contains four ready-to-edit routes. The complete
`example-collections-source.json` and `example-collections-plan.json` pair adds
List and Set products through the same compiler, editor and customer client.

## Read pages and preserve values

Results provide the declared columns, rows, row count and truncation state.
Redis text, stream IDs and score replies remain strings. Missing values use JSON
null. Binary values that are not valid UTF-8 use a `{ "base64": "..." }` object.
Redis sorted-set numeric representation and ordering continue to apply to score
values; the reader preserves their native textual reply.

When a stream entry repeats a field name, its projection uses that entry's last
value for the field. Stream results expose
`duplicateFieldProjection: "last-value"` with the returned rows.

Each request runs the fixed read-only projection script once. Projection and
native byte accounting happen inside Redis before selected values are returned
to the client. The declared `maxRows` is 1 for string and hash products and up to
1,000 for paged products. `maxBytes` is 1,024–917,504 bytes, and `timeoutMs` is
50–30,000 milliseconds. The complete JSON response also remains within the
selected byte limit. A result that exceeds either byte check returns
`QUERY_RESULT_TOO_LARGE`; the HTTP route uses status 413. Adjust the reviewed
projection or page size, or the declared byte limit, before requesting it again.

Declare `offset`, `after` or the set's required `cursor` to expose continuation for a paged product. Use the
returned `nextInput` as the next request's input. It retains the current
key-selection values and advances the declared
rank, list index, stream ID or native set cursor. A continuation is emitted only when it passes the same
input contract as a new request. If the next rank exceeds the declared offset
maximum, the response reports `continuationUnavailable: "OFFSET_LIMIT"`. A
cursor excluded by an enum or another declared input constraint reports
`continuationUnavailable: "INPUT_LIMIT"`. In either case `truncated` may still
be true because more source rows exist. The merchant can revise the reviewed
declaration to expose a wider range.

Each page is an individual live read. Changes to a sorted set or list between
requests can change positions; the stream cursor follows native stream IDs.
Set results expose `scanCursor`, `scanComplete`, `scanCount` and
`duplicatesPossible`. Follow `nextInput` even for an empty set page; native
ordering is unspecified and repeated members may occur across pages.
An oversized complete native scan batch returns HTTP 413 with
`QUERY_SCAN_PAGE_TOO_LARGE`. The reader preserves the native batch boundary;
use the selected source and cursor again after adjusting the declaration.
Release retention pins the reader configuration, while the Redis dataset
continues under its own operational lifecycle.

## Configure the native connection

The private `connection` selects one deployment. Omitted `topology` keeps the
original standalone profile. All native profiles accept `username`,
`passwordEnv`, `tls` and `caFile`. The host environment supplies the password
when a preview or seller starts. TLS defaults to `verify-full`, which validates
the server certificate and hostname. An explicit CA is relative to the source
file and is copied into prepared packages and retained releases.

| Deployment | Required connection fields | Database |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Standalone | `host`; optional `port` defaults to 6379 | `database` defaults to 0 |
| Cluster | `topology: "cluster"`, `rootNodes` | Database 0 |
| Sentinel | `topology: "sentinel"`, `name`, `sentinelRootNodes` | `database` defaults to 0 on the data server |

Start from the corresponding complete source and merchant-plan templates:

```sh
starforge redis init --directory /srv/merchant/cluster --topology cluster
starforge redis init --directory /srv/merchant/sentinel --topology sentinel
```

Each seed list contains 1–16 distinct `{ "host": "...", "port": 6379 }`
endpoints. Cluster seeds default to port 6379; Sentinel seeds default to 26379.
Use several independently reachable seeds so the driver can discover the
deployment when one seed is unavailable. `describe` reports the topology and
seed count without exposing hosts or credential values.

### Cluster

A Cluster connection uses the same merchant credentials and TLS settings for
seed discovery and every discovered data node:

```json
{
  "topology": "cluster",
  "rootNodes": [
    { "host": "redis-1.example", "port": 6379 },
    { "host": "redis-2.example", "port": 6379 },
    { "host": "redis-3.example", "port": 6379 }
  ],
  "username": "merchant",
  "passwordEnv": "REDIS_MERCHANT_PASSWORD",
  "tls": "verify-full"
}
```

Every declared product reads one selected Redis key. The driver receives that
key with the original `EVAL_RO` invocation, routes it to the slot's primary and
handles native `MOVED` and `ASK` redirects. The reader uses primary nodes.
Different products and enum-selected keys can occupy different slots. A Cluster
profile rejects nonzero databases before opening a connection.

### Sentinel

A Sentinel profile names the monitored primary and separates discovery
credentials and TLS from data credentials and TLS:

```json
{
  "topology": "sentinel",
  "name": "merchant-primary",
  "sentinelRootNodes": [
    { "host": "sentinel-1.example", "port": 26379 },
    { "host": "sentinel-2.example", "port": 26379 },
    { "host": "sentinel-3.example", "port": 26379 }
  ],
  "database": 0,
  "username": "merchant",
  "passwordEnv": "REDIS_MERCHANT_PASSWORD",
  "tls": "verify-full",
  "sentinelUsername": "merchant-monitor",
  "sentinelPasswordEnv": "REDIS_SENTINEL_PASSWORD",
  "sentinelTls": "verify-full"
}
```

`sentinelTls` also defaults to `verify-full`. Set `caFile` for a private
data-server CA and `sentinelCaFile` for a private Sentinel CA. Preparation
retains them independently as `database-ca.pem` and `sentinel-ca.pem` and
lists both required environment names in the manifest. The saved workspace
retains the original certificate bytes and environment references through
reopen, customer preparation and release staging.

The native Sentinel client discovers and reads the current primary. Its
existing topology refresh handles a promoted primary; this reader does not
select replicas. Supply monitor credentials for the Sentinel service and data
credentials for the database nodes. Configure each service through its own
existing administration interface.

### Advertised addresses and local receiving

Cluster and Sentinel deployments may advertise addresses that differ from the
host's reachable addresses. An optional `nodeAddressMap` translates exact
advertised `host:port` strings to explicit endpoints:

```json
{
  "nodeAddressMap": {
    "10.20.0.12:6379": { "host": "redis-2.internal.example", "port": 6379 }
  }
}
```

The map permits at most 256 entries. Each destination specifies its port.
Sentinel applies the same map to discovered monitor and data endpoints. Keep the
mapped endpoint compatible with its server certificate and the host's existing
network access.

For a local development deployment, explicitly choose `local-plaintext`.
If either the data or Sentinel connection uses this mode, every seed, mapped
endpoint and discovered destination must be `127.0.0.1`, `::1` or
`localhost`. The source checks discovered destinations as well as the initial
profile. Use the verified TLS profiles for a remote deployment.

### Connection lifetime

The source has explicit `maxConnections`, `maxPending`, `connectTimeoutMs`,
`idleTimeoutMs` and `startupTimeoutMs`. For Cluster and Sentinel,
`maxConnections` counts owned logical clients; the native driver opens the
sockets needed for discovery and data nodes inside each client. Size this limit
alongside the deployment's socket capacity. The default is four logical clients.

The source reuses ready clients and keeps requests within the configured queue
and lifetime. On cancellation or deadline it retires the affected client and
joins its connection and command work before releasing its pool slot. Closing
the source joins all retiring clients as well as active work. A failed seed can
fall through to another configured seed using the native driver.

A client deadline ends the reader's request; a script already executing on
Redis continues according to the server's script lifecycle. Stopping a seller
uses the existing HTTP drain before closing its source.

## Grant the command and key permissions

The merchant identity needs `+eval_ro` and `+ping`, plus the commands used by its
declared products: `+get`, `+strlen`, `+hmget`, `+hstrlen`, `+zrange`, and
`+xrange`. Selecting a nonzero database also requires `+select`. Restrict its key
permissions to the fixed merchant keys represented by the source declarations.

For an existing dedicated merchant user whose password is already configured,
the example source uses this ACL permission fragment:

```text
ACL SETUSER merchant on resetkeys -@all ~merchant:availability:catalog ~merchant:catalog:north ~merchant:catalog:south ~merchant:rankings:daily ~merchant:events +eval_ro +ping +get +strlen +hmget +hstrlen +zrange +xrange
```

List products additionally require `+lrange` and `+llen`; Set products require
`+sscan`. Add the declared collection keys to the same merchant key rules. The
[collection guide](COLLECTIONS.md#native-access) gives the complete permission
fragment for its example source.

For Cluster, add `+cluster|slots` for native discovery and `+asking` for a
read redirected during a slot migration. Apply the merchant identity and its
key permissions consistently to the Cluster's data nodes.

For Sentinel, configure the separate monitor reader with `+ping`,
`+sentinel|master`, `+sentinel|replicas`, `+sentinel|sentinels`,
`+psubscribe` and `+punsubscribe`, together with channel access for native
topology notifications. The integration fixture uses `&*` for that monitor
identity. The data-server merchant retains the read permissions above. Sentinel
administration and failover use the deployment's existing administrator identity.

Apply the equivalent settings through the database's existing administration
interface. Native script execution respects the user's command and key
permissions. Redis-compatible hosted providers must expose the same read-only
script capability for this source.

Primary command and access-control references:

- [Redis EVAL_RO](https://redis.io/docs/latest/commands/eval_ro/)
- [Valkey EVAL_RO](https://valkey.io/commands/eval_ro/)
- [Redis ACL](https://redis.io/docs/latest/operate/oss_and_stack/management/security/acl/)
- [node-redis 6.2.1 Cluster](https://github.com/redis/node-redis/blob/redis%406.2.1/docs/clustering.md)
- [node-redis 6.2.1 Sentinel](https://github.com/redis/node-redis/blob/redis%406.2.1/docs/sentinel.md)

## Operate the service and retained releases

`start` and `serve` accept `--max-in-flight`, `--drain-grace-ms`, and
`--availability-dir` for the existing seller controls. `--no-operations` runs
only the seller listener. An explicitly selected loopback HTTP facilitator uses
`--allow-local-facilitator`; normal facilitator URLs use HTTPS.

The same prepared package can be retained, compared, activated and rolled back
through `starforge releases stage --redis-package PREPARED_DIRECTORY`. The
existing release console operates the actual retained source and original
seller. See [Redis releases](../../sf82-seller-pilot/REDIS_RELEASES.md) for the
complete package-to-release workflow.

The retained generated client includes its original `client-export.json`
manifest alongside the JavaScript, TypeScript, OpenAPI, package and README
files. Preparation hashes all six client files, and release staging carries
them together for the original client inspection and download flow.

Embedded consumers can use `openRedisSourceFile`, `prepareRedisSeller`,
`verifyPreparedRedisSeller`, `startRedisSeller`, `bindRedisSeller` and
`createRedisNativeFactory`. The source owns Redis queries and connection
lifetime; the existing SF30 seller and SF82 manager own payment, service and
release operation.

## Native integration journey

Run `node native-journey.mjs` from this directory after installing the selected
native runtime. `REDIS_SERVER` selects an installed Redis 7+ executable; its
shared libraries must already be available to the process. The journey creates
an isolated loopback Redis database, exercises the four read products through
an ACL user, exports the original customer client, and uses the original buyer
and SF82 child process for upgrade and rollback. Its facilitator is the existing
local x402 protocol fixture. `SF30_REDIS_JOURNEY_OUTPUT` optionally saves the
result to a selected file.

Set `SF30_REDIS_JOURNEY_TOPOLOGY=cluster` for three native primaries, live slot
routing and a slot migration, or `SF30_REDIS_JOURNEY_TOPOLOGY=sentinel` for an
authenticated primary/replica deployment and three Sentinel monitors with an
actual primary promotion. These modes continue through the same declared
products, merchant, buyer, customer files and retained release journey. Add

// MIT. One fixed Redis/Valkey EVAL_RO script. Buyers supply typed values, never code.
// Projection and byte accounting happen before any database value crosses the wire.
export const READ_SCRIPT = `
local kind, count, budget, position = ARGV[1], tonumber(ARGV[2]), tonumber(ARGV[3]), ARGV[4]
local rows, used, truncated = {}, 0, 0
local function keep(value)
  if type(value) == 'string' then
    used = used + string.len(value)
    if used > budget then error('SF30_RESULT_TOO_LARGE') end
  end
  return value
end
if kind == 'get' then
  if redis.call('STRLEN', KEYS[1]) > budget then error('SF30_RESULT_TOO_LARGE') end
  rows[1] = {keep(redis.call('GET', KEYS[1]))}
elseif kind == 'hash' then
  local size, fields = 0, {}
  for i = 5, #ARGV do
    size = size + redis.call('HSTRLEN', KEYS[1], ARGV[i])
    if size > budget then error('SF30_RESULT_TOO_LARGE') end
    fields[#fields + 1] = ARGV[i]
  end
  local values = redis.call('HMGET', KEYS[1], unpack(fields))
  for i = 1, #values do keep(values[i]) end
  rows[1] = values
elseif kind == 'list' then
  local start = tonumber(position)
  local values = redis.call('LRANGE', KEYS[1], position, tostring(start + count - 1))
  for i = 1, #values do rows[#rows + 1] = {tostring(start + i - 1), keep(values[i])} end
  if redis.call('LLEN', KEYS[1]) > start + #values then truncated = 1 end
elseif kind == 'set' then
  -- COUNT is a work hint, not a row limit. Return a whole native batch or fail:
  -- slicing it while advancing the native cursor would silently skip members.
  local page = redis.call('SSCAN', KEYS[1], position, 'COUNT', ARGV[5])
  if #page[2] > count then error('SF30_SCAN_PAGE_TOO_MANY_ROWS') end
  for i = 1, #page[2] do rows[#rows + 1] = {keep(page[2][i])} end
  if page[1] ~= '0' then truncated = 1 end
  return {truncated, rows, page[1]}
elseif kind == 'sorted-set' then
  local start = tonumber(position)
  for offset = start, start + count do
    local pair = redis.call('ZRANGE', KEYS[1], tostring(offset), tostring(offset), 'WITHSCORES')
    if #pair == 0 then break end
    if offset == start + count then truncated = 1; break end
    rows[#rows + 1] = {keep(pair[1]), keep(pair[2])}
  end
elseif kind == 'stream' then
  local cursor = position == '-' and '-' or '(' .. position
  for i = 1, count + 1 do
    local entries = redis.call('XRANGE', KEYS[1], cursor, '+', 'COUNT', 1)
    if #entries == 0 then break end
    if i > count then truncated = 1; break end
    local entry, selected = entries[1], {}
    for j = 1, #entry[2], 2 do selected[entry[2][j]] = entry[2][j + 1] end
    local row = {keep(entry[1])}
    for j = 5, #ARGV do row[#row + 1] = keep(selected[ARGV[j]] or false) end
    rows[#rows + 1] = row
    cursor = '(' .. entry[1]
  end
else error('SF30_QUERY_KIND_INVALID') end
return {truncated, rows}
`;


## 2. Choose the customer's budget and initial inputs

Copy customer-export.plan.example.json to a customer-owned working path. Choose a stable operationId for this one business export and inspect every selected product and initial input.

The included example selects a maximum of **60 buyer calls**, **10,000 atomic units per call**, and **600,000 atomic units in aggregate**, matching the supplied example merchant's advertised amount. Those numbers are configuration values to review against the actual selected asset and use case. Atomic amounts are decimal strings throughout.

maxCalls is the maximum number of original buyer delegations, from 1 to 100,000. A budget smaller than the selected product count intentionally permits only that many calls. The application visits each product once before continuing paginated products in rounds. Every delegation reserves its permitted atomic ceiling against the aggregate budget before it calls the buyer. This conservative total includes calls whose outcome later requires review. The manifest separately records amounts present in returned native requirements; that field describes the returned requirements.

Each product explicitly selects acceptIndex and paymentFlow. The original generated client enforces the selected advertised payment identity, and the original buyer reviews the fresh challenge. The application also requires the same network and asset across all selected products so an aggregate atomic budget has one meaning.

The response limit applies to the full bytes exposed by Fetch. The example permits 1 MiB per response and a 30-second response-file transfer. The original buyer/transport owns its request timeout and external cancellation policy.

# Receive an application contract across Redis and Valkey

This command joins the original commissioning engine to receive the same customer application on a baseline Redis deployment and a selected Valkey deployment. Each side keeps its original saved source workspace, revision, preview operations, complete response pages, package and generated customer files.

The paired input identifies the agreed source edition or receiving window. The command checks the same declared queries, routes, payment terms and customer examples on both sources. It compares complete original rows, writes useful row differences, and can stage the candidate package after both customer expectations and the paired comparison match.

## Prepare the selected input

From the installed source directory:

~~~sh
node sf30-seller-sdk/redis/workspace/cutover.mjs template > customer-cutover.json
node sf30-seller-sdk/redis/workspace/cutover.mjs review --input customer-cutover.json
~~~

The complete example is a starting contract for the original six product kinds. Replace its connection, source edition, operator, key/field declarations, product terms and expected results with the customer's selected values. The template's example hosts and REPLACE_WITH labels are editable placeholders. Read the original [commissioning guide](COMMISSIONING.md) and [connection setup](SETUP.md) for each source profile.

The schema is stellar-forge.redis-cutover-input.v1:

| Field | Selected meaning |
|---|---|
| operationId | The stable paired receiving operation. |
| consistency | immutable-edition or paused-writes, the customer's actual edition/window reference, and receiving operator. |
| baseline | Complete original stellar-forge.redis-commissioning-input.v1 for the Redis source. |
| candidate | Complete original commissioning input for the Valkey source, with distinct creation and receiving IDs. |
| comparisons | One explicit rule for each original check ID. |
| release | Optional original candidate release ID/runtime, staged after the comparison passes. |
| maxComparisonBytes | Combined original row JSON budget for one comparison; default 64 MiB, selectable 1–256 MiB. |

Both original commissioning inputs retain identical queries, routes, payment terms and checks. Their actual connection profiles, source pool/timeouts, public receiving origins, workspace labels and public CA material can differ. Keep private passwords in the named environment variables. Retain distinct monitor/data CAs and credentials when the selected deployment uses Sentinel. The ordinary original setup API carries CA files into each saved source.

A receiving window is an operator-supplied data condition. The command records the selected reference and the actual observation time of every native page. The customer's datastore operator establishes and releases that window. The application command reads and prepares application artifacts.

Place an optional release at the top level. The two nested inputs omit release, allowing the paired result to determine when the candidate package is staged. Activation and external traffic selection remain ordinary explicit operator actions on that retained release.

## Compare the application semantics

- **Ordered:** current values, projected hash rows, rankings, streams and lists retain exact canonical row order and values. A mismatch lists every changed, inserted or removed row index. The original list/stream/ranking kinds require ordered comparison.
- **Multiset:** an explicitly unordered non-set result compares row values and their occurrence counts. Duplicate values remain meaningful.
- **Set:** the original set query compares membership. Redis/Valkey SSCAN can visit a member more than once and returns an unspecified order. Only the comparison view removes repeat visits; each original response, row count, cursor and page remains preserved.

Collection checks receive all pages. They follow the original nextInput until completion, including empty SSCAN pages with a nonterminal cursor. Native uint64 cursors stay decimal strings. A row or page budget ends receiving with the original incomplete-operation details. The tool validates every saved page against its original completed preview, query, revision, input, full-result hash and aggregate rows before computing differences.

Use customer-specific expected values alongside the paired comparison. For a set, expected.columns and useful requiredRows avoid treating unspecified native scan order as part of membership. Exact native row counts remain available when the customer's contract calls for them.

## Receive and reopen

Use a parent directory with sufficient space for both original saved workspaces and their complete prepared packages:

~~~sh
umask 077
node sf30-seller-sdk/redis/workspace/cutover.mjs receive \
  --input customer-cutover.json --directory /private/customer-cutover
~~~

The command completes baseline receiving, candidate receiving, row comparison, original customer package verification and optional candidate staging. RECEIVED exits zero. CONTRACT_MISMATCH exits two and preserves both original receiving outcomes and full row differences. Operational failures exit one with the original error and retained receiving location.

The directory contains:

- cutover-input.json: the complete frozen input and its original SHA256.
- baseline/ and candidate/: the original native authoring workspaces.
- baseline-receiving.json and candidate-receiving.json: complete original commissioning outcomes.
- difference-CHECKID.json: full ordered changes or membership/count differences, column comparison and customer expectation results.
- cutover-result.json: the comparison summary, exact difference hashes, observation windows, original workspace bindings, candidate/baseline customer package references and selected release.
- cutover-error.json: the most recent interrupted/failed invocation details, if one occurred.

Cold comparison uses the full original saved pages:

~~~sh
node sf30-seller-sdk/redis/workspace/cutover.mjs compare \
  --input customer-cutover.json --directory /private/customer-cutover
~~~

The comparison reopens the exact workspace/profile/revision bindings. It uses existing saved read outcomes and the same retained candidate release request. Credentials are needed for native receiving; saved comparison can operate from retained rows. When a previous native operation was interrupted, rerun receive with the identical input and directory to let the original commissioning engine recover its existing request IDs.

After a source or contract correction, choose a new paired operation and directory, with new baseline/candidate creation/receiving IDs. Preserve the earlier comparison as the previous receiving edition. A repeated original request deliberately returns its retained result; it does not silently take a new observation of changed customer data.

Optional offline workspace creation uses create with the same input/directory. Its created JSON artifacts preserve prior complete receiving reports.

## Customer operation and handover

Each successful side has the original generated Node client and OpenAPI from its saved package. The candidate is the selected application handover; the baseline preserves the original client/contract reference. The [customer exporter](CUSTOMER_EXPORT.md) runs selected actual operation IDs with an explicit payment budget and retains full paid response pages before continuing.

The source/browser/MCP/managed Applications continue to use the original workspace directories. The paired tool adds no second customer database or background queue.

The handover includes the original source edition/window, both source profiles with environment references, exact expected/observed comparison, useful differences and their resolution, generated customer files, selected release and rollback edition, and the named customer receiving operator. Datastore migration, replication, traffic change and production rollout follow that operator's actual selected plan.

## Programmatic API

~~~js
import {
  normalizeRedisCutover, receiveRedisCutover, compareRedisCutoverRows
} from './sf30-seller-sdk/redis/workspace/cutover.mjs';

const review = normalizeRedisCutover(input, process.env);
const result = await receiveRedisCutover({
  input, directory: '/private/customer-cutover',
  environment: process.env, mode: 'receive'
});
~~~

receiveRedisCutover accepts review, create, receive or compare. Supply inputSha256 when receiving a previously selected complete input file; otherwise the API uses canonical JSON. The CLI pins the full input bytes. Keep that same input representation when reopening its original directory.

compareRedisCutoverRows exposes the same exact comparison for an existing operator view. The full receiving API verifies original native page custody before using it.
